bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Systemic receivable cycles across state-level agencies — Turnkey public-utility engineering is exposed to the timing of state budgetary allocations and bureaucratic approval windows; during FY26 industry-wide delays in state fund releases under rural piped-water programmes moderated billing velocity and stretched receivables beyond historic averages. Management's mitigation is a pivot to front-loaded payment structures in newer contracts and use of newly injected State Revival funds to clear backlogged cycles.
- Early expense booking and working-capital drag — Multi-year infrastructure contracts require continuous construction progress to avoid default or performance penalties, so delays in government cash clearances force early expense booking and deployment of internal capital to sustain site velocity. Management leans on a consolidated net debt-to-equity ratio of 0.03x and a Rs 808 crore equity base rather than expanding expensive debt.
- Input commodity volatility and inflationary margin pressure — Turnkey EPC operations are structurally sensitive to prices of structural steel, cement, aggregates and specialised alloy components; on long-gestation orders sharp inflationary spikes risk compressing projected EBITDA margins. Mitigation is price-escalation clauses indexed to wholesale price benchmarks in new tenders.
- Extended litigation cycles for arbitration recoveries — Government departments frequently contest tribunal declarations through the High Courts and the Supreme Court, so the substantial monetary upside from outstanding awards (including the Rs 587 crore Jaipur-Bhilwara Toll Road award and the Rs 53 crore Gurha Thermal award) faces long delays before converting into operational cash. The Company runs a dedicated legal cell and files executing petitions to fast-track court-mandated deposits.
- Complex terrains, logistical bottlenecks and climate risk — Building hydro installations and dams in high-altitude zones, remote river valleys and border corridors brings unpredictable subterranean anomalies and severe logistics constraints, while more frequent extreme weather (flash floods, delayed monsoons) can disrupt sites and river-diversion works. Mitigation rests on over 50 years of technical data, in-house R&D, pre-bidding topological mapping and specialised engineering protocols.
- Intense competition in standard civil bidding — Entry of multiple domestic and international players into standard civil engineering contracts has intensified competitive bidding and compressed margins locally; the Company is consciously moving away from low-margin un-segregated civil construction toward niche, high-entry-barrier domains such as Pumped Storage Projects and integrated hydro-mechanical setups where technical pre-qualifications are required.
- Project delays and cost overruns on large civil works — Flagged under Threats: land acquisition issues, regulatory hurdles, environmental clearances and unforeseen geological conditions can cause delays, cost escalation and profitability impact; environmental and social scrutiny of large dam projects can add protests and further delay, and skilled-labour availability for specialised dam and gate construction remains a constraint.
- Qualified audit opinion on the standalone financial statements — The statutory auditor issued a qualified opinion on the standalone financial statements of Om Infra Limited (which include its 9 joint operations) for the year ended 31 March 2026, together with an Emphasis of Matter; the text of the basis for the qualification and of the emphasis items is cut off in the routed extract, so the specific matters cannot be read from this bundle.

business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body: The Company operates an integrated, turnkey execution architecture across two prime business landscapes. In Water Infrastructure and Heavy Engineering it provides turnkey execution from design and detail engineering, through precision fabrication, to installation, testing and commissioning of hydro-mechanical projects, irrigation systems, dams and piped water networks for government and state water agencies. In Real Estate Development it builds high-value residential townships, commercial assets and urban redevelopment projects, backed by its internal engineering and civil execution capability.

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Om Infra's expansion is order-book and project driven rather than plant driven; the routed sections describe no manufacturing capacity addition and state that there have been no changes in the business carried on by the Company or its subsidiaries. In the Engineering & Infrastructure division the defining event of the year was the Isarda Dam Project (value Rs 615.17 Crores, with an additional scope of Rs 48 crore allotted), where water impounding commenced on July 30, 2025 following government approval on July 25th - the first time since construction began - on a 6.03 km composite dam structure with 3.24 TMC of Phase 1 and 10.77 TMC of Phase 2 capacity, serving drinking water supply under JJM and ERCP integration for over 3 crore people across 13 districts. The division also secured a Rs 129 crore municipal order from Uttar Pradesh Jal Nigam (Urban), Shahjahanpur, for end-to-end water infrastructure and PLS SCADA automation, and carried an unexecuted order book of Rs 2,107 Crores as of March 31, 2026 (Rs 1,351 Cr from the Jal Jeevan Mission and Rs 756 Cr from hydro-mechanical components in dams), on a base of more than 70 civil and hydro-mechanical contracts executed over the last five decades. Forward footprint expansion is framed as bidding rather than capital deployment: management is target-bidding components of the emerging Eastern Rajasthan Canal Project (ERCP) and has set a standalone fresh order inflow threshold of Rs 1,500 crore for FY2026-27, aimed at hydro-mechanical, pumped storage, STP and water infrastructure projects, leveraging its delivery of the Kundah PSP (1,000 MW). In Real Estate the strategy is monetisation and asset-light development rather than fresh capex: Pallacia (Jaipur, project area 646150 sq. ft.) has recognised cumulative revenue of Rs 275 Crores with Rs 290 Crores of remaining realisable value; Om Green Meadows (Kota, project area 353814 sq. ft.) has recognised Rs 63 Crores with Rs 24 Crores remaining; and at the Bandra SRA project in Mumbai all long-standing land clearances and MHADA disputes are resolved, with joint-venture partner Valor Estate Ltd having commenced site survey layout planning to fast-track development without further capital call-downs from the Company. The execution roadmap table lists Meadows (Kota, housing, 338 units, 4,45,972 sq. ft.), Pallacia (Jaipur, housing, 152 units, 6,46,150 sq. ft.) and Bandra Reclamation MHADA (Mumbai, with DB Realty and others, housing, approximately 2,50,000 sq. ft. OMIL share), alongside land parcels at VKIA Jaipur, Kota and Jaipur. Non-core asset recovery runs in parallel, with arbitration awards of Rs 587 Crores (Bhilwara Jaipur Toll Road, in the Rajasthan High Court, 10% of the award already received) and Rs 53 Crores (Gurha Thermal Power, pending in the Supreme Court) expected to contribute about Rs 700+ crores of realisations over the next 2-3 years.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- A Central Government infrastructure push with a national outlay scaling to Rs 12.2 lakh crore, placing the Company at the intersection of water infrastructure, heavy hydro-mechanical engineering and urban real estate.
- Extension of JJM 2.0 till 2028 within a total water sector outlay of over Rs 84,000 crore - Rs 67,670 crore for the Jal Jeevan Mission, Rs 8,000 crore for AMRUT 2.0, Rs 5,226 crore for river interlinking and irrigation and Rs 3,100 crore for the National Ganga Plan.
- Suspension of the Indus Water Treaty fast-tracking regional hydro project execution and boosting heavy engineering pipeline requirements in bordering regions.
- A targeted domestic pipeline of 50+ GW of planned pumped storage configurations, described as a multi-decade market opportunity, with the Company bidding on the back of its 1,000 MW Kundah PSP credentials.
- Risk Fund support de-risking execution and improving project timelines, and Viksit Bharat capex momentum providing multi-year demand visibility.
- FY26 billing velocity was consciously moderated during industry-wide procedural funding delays under state-level rural piped-water packages, which elongated working capital cycles for up to nine months; liquidity improved in the second half after state-level economic revival allocations totalling Rs 27,000 crores across Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan, with milestone collections structured to flow systematically into Q1FY27.
- Margin levers into FY27: optimised internal component production, stabilisation of input material indexes and a higher proportion of complex, high-margin hydro engineering milestones.
- Real estate demand driven by steady premiumization and resilient residential and commercial demand across Tier-1 and Tier-2 urban corridors, with internal civil execution capabilities acting as a shield protecting overall margins across active regional townships.
- A shift in the domestic market toward high-margin clean energy alternatives, plus mega-scale river interlinking and cross-basin water transfer channelization such as the ERCP, as structural order inflow drivers.
- Unexecuted order book of Rs 2,107 crore as at 31 March 2026, providing extensive multi-year revenue visibility.
- Order book composition: Rs 1,351 crore from the Jal Jeevan Mission and Rs 756 crore from hydro-mechanical components in dams.
- The Engineering & Infrastructure segment accounts for 100% of the active unexecuted project order book (stated at Rs 2,106.61 crore as of March 31, 2026).
- New win during the year: a municipal order worth Rs 129 crore from Uttar Pradesh Jal Nigam (Urban), Shahjahanpur, for end-to-end water infrastructure and PLS SCADA automation.
- Isarda Dam Project valued at Rs 615.17 crore with additional scope of Rs 48 crore allotted; water impounding commenced on July 30, 2025.
- Fresh order intake target of Rs 1,500 crore for FY27, focused on hydro-mechanical, pumped storage, STP and water infrastructure projects.
- Active bidding intention of up to Rs 2,000 crore in the Eastern Rajasthan Canal Project corridor alone.
- Real estate monetisation pipeline exceeding Rs 600 crore, with Rs 290 crore of remaining realisable value at Pallacia (Jaipur) and Rs 24 crore at Om Green Meadows (Kota).

currentContext.expansion: Om Infra's expansion is order-book and project driven rather than plant driven; the routed sections describe no manufacturing capacity addition and state that there have been no changes in the business carried on by the Company or its subsidiaries. In the Engineering & Infrastructure division the defining event of the year was the Isarda Dam Project (value Rs 615.17 Crores, with an additional scope of Rs 48 crore allotted), where water impounding commenced on July 30, 2025 following government approval on July 25th - the first time since construction began - on a 6.03 km composite dam structure with 3.24 TMC of Phase 1 and 10.77 TMC of Phase 2 capacity, serving drinking water supply under JJM and ERCP integration for over 3 crore people across 13 districts. The division also secured a Rs 129 crore municipal order from Uttar Pradesh Jal Nigam (Urban), Shahjahanpur, for end-to-end water infrastructure and PLS SCADA automation, and carried an unexecuted order book of Rs 2,107 Crores as of March 31, 2026 (Rs 1,351 Cr from the Jal Jeevan Mission and Rs 756 Cr from hydro-mechanical components in dams), on a base of more than 70 civil and hydro-mechanical contracts executed over the last five decades. Forward footprint expansion is framed as bidding rather than capital deployment: management is target-bidding components of the emerging Eastern Rajasthan Canal Project (ERCP) and has set a standalone fresh order inflow threshold of Rs 1,500 crore for FY2026-27, aimed at hydro-mechanical, pumped storage, STP and water infrastructure projects, leveraging its delivery of the Kundah PSP (1,000 MW). In Real Estate the strategy is monetisation and asset-light development rather than fresh capex: Pallacia (Jaipur, project area 646150 sq. ft.) has recognised cumulative revenue of Rs 275 Crores with Rs 290 Crores of remaining realisable value; Om Green Meadows (Kota, project area 353814 sq. ft.) has recognised Rs 63 Crores with Rs 24 Crores remaining; and at the Bandra SRA project in Mumbai all long-standing land clearances and MHADA disputes are resolved, with joint-venture partner Valor Estate Ltd having commenced site survey layout planning to fast-track development without further capital call-downs from the Company. The execution roadmap table lists Meadows (Kota, housing, 338 units, 4,45,972 sq. ft.), Pallacia (Jaipur, housing, 152 units, 6,46,150 sq. ft.) and Bandra Reclamation MHADA (Mumbai, with DB Realty and others, housing, approximately 2,50,000 sq. ft. OMIL share), alongside land parcels at VKIA Jaipur, Kota and Jaipur. Non-core asset recovery runs in parallel, with arbitration awards of Rs 587 Crores (Bhilwara Jaipur Toll Road, in the Rajasthan High Court, 10% of the award already received) and Rs 53 Crores (Gurha Thermal Power, pending in the Supreme Court) expected to contribute about Rs 700+ crores of realisations over the next 2-3 years.

risks.risk: Systemic receivable cycles across state-level agencies
risks.note: Turnkey public-utility engineering is exposed to the timing of state budgetary allocations and bureaucratic approval windows; during FY26 industry-wide delays in state fund releases under rural piped-water programmes moderated billing velocity and stretched receivables beyond historic averages. Management's mitigation is a pivot to front-loaded payment structures in newer contracts and use of newly injected State Revival funds to clear backlogged cycles.

risks.risk: Early expense booking and working-capital drag
risks.note: Multi-year infrastructure contracts require continuous construction progress to avoid default or performance penalties, so delays in government cash clearances force early expense booking and deployment of internal capital to sustain site velocity. Management leans on a consolidated net debt-to-equity ratio of 0.03x and a Rs 808 crore equity base rather than expanding expensive debt.

risks.risk: Input commodity volatility and inflationary margin pressure
risks.note: Turnkey EPC operations are structurally sensitive to prices of structural steel, cement, aggregates and specialised alloy components; on long-gestation orders sharp inflationary spikes risk compressing projected EBITDA margins. Mitigation is price-escalation clauses indexed to wholesale price benchmarks in new tenders.

risks.risk: Extended litigation cycles for arbitration recoveries
risks.note: Government departments frequently contest tribunal declarations through the High Courts and the Supreme Court, so the substantial monetary upside from outstanding awards (including the Rs 587 crore Jaipur-Bhilwara Toll Road award and the Rs 53 crore Gurha Thermal award) faces long delays before converting into operational cash. The Company runs a dedicated legal cell and files executing petitions to fast-track court-mandated deposits.

risks.risk: Complex terrains, logistical bottlenecks and climate risk
risks.note: Building hydro installations and dams in high-altitude zones, remote river valleys and border corridors brings unpredictable subterranean anomalies and severe logistics constraints, while more frequent extreme weather (flash floods, delayed monsoons) can disrupt sites and river-diversion works. Mitigation rests on over 50 years of technical data, in-house R&D, pre-bidding topological mapping and specialised engineering protocols.

risks.risk: Intense competition in standard civil bidding
risks.note: Entry of multiple domestic and international players into standard civil engineering contracts has intensified competitive bidding and compressed margins locally; the Company is consciously moving away from low-margin un-segregated civil construction toward niche, high-entry-barrier domains such as Pumped Storage Projects and integrated hydro-mechanical setups where technical pre-qualifications are required.

risks.risk: Project delays and cost overruns on large civil works
risks.note: Flagged under Threats: land acquisition issues, regulatory hurdles, environmental clearances and unforeseen geological conditions can cause delays, cost escalation and profitability impact; environmental and social scrutiny of large dam projects can add protests and further delay, and skilled-labour availability for specialised dam and gate construction remains a constraint.

demand_drivers.body:
- A Central Government infrastructure push with a national outlay scaling to Rs 12.2 lakh crore, placing the Company at the intersection of water infrastructure, heavy hydro-mechanical engineering and urban real estate.
- Extension of JJM 2.0 till 2028 within a total water sector outlay of over Rs 84,000 crore - Rs 67,670 crore for the Jal Jeevan Mission, Rs 8,000 crore for AMRUT 2.0, Rs 5,226 crore for river interlinking and irrigation and Rs 3,100 crore for the National Ganga Plan.
- Suspension of the Indus Water Treaty fast-tracking regional hydro project execution and boosting heavy engineering pipeline requirements in bordering regions.
- A targeted domestic pipeline of 50+ GW of planned pumped storage configurations, described as a multi-decade market opportunity, with the Company bidding on the back of its 1,000 MW Kundah PSP credentials.
- Risk Fund support de-risking execution and improving project timelines, and Viksit Bharat capex momentum providing multi-year demand visibility.

- Margin levers into FY27: optimised internal component production, stabilisation of input material indexes and a higher proportion of complex, high-margin hydro engineering milestones.
- Real estate demand driven by steady premiumization and resilient residential and commercial demand across Tier-1 and Tier-2 urban corridors, with internal civil execution capabilities acting as a shield protecting overall margins across active regional townships.
- A shift in the domestic market toward high-margin clean energy alternatives, plus mega-scale river interlinking and cross-basin water transfer channelization such as the ERCP, as structural order inflow drivers.
- Unexecuted order book of Rs 2,107 crore as at 31 March 2026, providing extensive multi-year revenue visibility.
- Order book composition: Rs 1,351 crore from the Jal Jeevan Mission and Rs 756 crore from hydro-mechanical components in dams.
- The Engineering & Infrastructure segment accounts for 100% of the active unexecuted project order book (stated at Rs 2,106.61 crore as of March 31, 2026).
- New win during the year: a municipal order worth Rs 129 crore from Uttar Pradesh Jal Nigam (Urban), Shahjahanpur, for end-to-end water infrastructure and PLS SCADA automation.
- Isarda Dam Project valued at Rs 615.17 crore with additional scope of Rs 48 crore allotted; water impounding commenced on July 30, 2025.
- Fresh order intake target of Rs 1,500 crore for FY27, focused on hydro-mechanical, pumped storage, STP and water infrastructure projects.
- Active bidding intention of up to Rs 2,000 crore in the Eastern Rajasthan Canal Project corridor alone.
- Real estate monetisation pipeline exceeding Rs 600 crore, with Rs 290 crore of remaining realisable value at Pallacia (Jaipur) and Rs 24 crore at Om Green Meadows (Kota).

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Om Infra's expansion is order-book and project driven rather than plant driven; the routed sections describe no manufacturing capacity addition and state that there have been no changes in the business carried on by the Company or its subsidiaries. In the Engineering & Infrastructure division the defining event of the year was the Isarda Dam Project (value Rs 615.17 Crores, with an additional scope of Rs 48 crore allotted), where water impounding commenced on July 30, 2025 following government approval on July 25th - the first time since construction began - on a 6.03 km composite dam structure with 3.24 TMC of Phase 1 and 10.77 TMC of Phase 2 capacity, serving drinking water supply under JJM and ERCP integration for over 3 crore people across 13 districts. The division also secured a Rs 129 crore municipal order from Uttar Pradesh Jal Nigam (Urban), Shahjahanpur, for end-to-end water infrastructure and PLS SCADA automation, and carried an unexecuted order book of Rs 2,107 Crores as of March 31, 2026 (Rs 1,351 Cr from the Jal Jeevan Mission and Rs 756 Cr from hydro-mechanical components in dams), on a base of more than 70 civil and hydro-mechanical contracts executed over the last five decades. Forward footprint expansion is framed as bidding rather than capital deployment: management is target-bidding components of the emerging Eastern Rajasthan Canal Project (ERCP) and has set a standalone fresh order inflow threshold of Rs 1,500 crore for FY2026-27, aimed at hydro-mechanical, pumped storage, STP and water infrastructure projects, leveraging its delivery of the Kundah PSP (1,000 MW). In Real Estate the strategy is monetisation and asset-light development rather than fresh capex: Pallacia (Jaipur, project area 646150 sq. ft.) has recognised cumulative revenue of Rs 275 Crores with Rs 290 Crores of remaining realisable value; Om Green Meadows (Kota, project area 353814 sq. ft.) has recognised Rs 63 Crores with Rs 24 Crores remaining; and at the Bandra SRA project in Mumbai all long-standing land clearances and MHADA disputes are resolved, with joint-venture partner Valor Estate Ltd having commenced site survey layout planning to fast-track development without further capital call-downs from the Company. The execution roadmap table lists Meadows (Kota, housing, 338 units, 4,45,972 sq. ft.), Pallacia (Jaipur, housing, 152 units, 6,46,150 sq. ft.) and Bandra Reclamation MHADA (Mumbai, with DB Realty and others, housing, approximately 2,50,000 sq. ft. OMIL share), alongside land parcels at VKIA Jaipur, Kota and Jaipur. Non-core asset recovery runs in parallel, with arbitration awards of Rs 587 Crores (Bhilwara Jaipur Toll Road, in the Rajasthan High Court, 10% of the award already received) and Rs 53 Crores (Gurha Thermal Power, pending in the Supreme Court) expected to contribute about Rs 700+ crores of realisations over the next 2-3 years.

moat.body:

- High entry barriers in its core niche - strict technical pre-qualifications for hydro-mechanical gates, penstocks and hoists eliminate unorganised competition
- Integrated turnkey capability spanning design, detail engineering, precision fabrication, installation, testing and commissioning, in an industry shifting from fragmented execution to whole-lifecycle players
- Credentialing from execution at the Kundah Pumped Storage Project (1,000 MW), used to bid for the national PSP and grid-storage pipeline
- Order-book visibility of Rs 2,107 crore of unexecuted orders as at 31 March 2026, comprising Rs 1,351 crore from the Jal Jeevan Mission and Rs 756 crore from dam hydro-mechanical components
- Conservative balance sheet - consolidated net worth of Rs 808 crore and a net debt-to-equity ratio of 0.03x, used to absorb receivable timing mismatches without expensive debt
- In-house civil and engineering execution acts as a margin shield in the real estate segment against volatile material cost indices
- Non-dilutive latent value in arbitration awards and non-core assets, alongside an asset-light Mumbai SRA structure requiring no further capital deployment by the Company

themes.title: Water & environmental-infra EPC
themes.need: AMRUT, Namami Gange and Jal Jeevan still define the pipeline, but Q1FY27 put a number on the funding freeze. WPIL's consolidated revenue rose 32% to INR 501cr while STANDALONE collapsed 37% to INR 115cr as domestic Jal Jeevan invoicing froze, with INR 300-350cr of JJM receivables pending (mostly West Bengal, some MP) and nil received in the quarter - management expects substantial inflow only in Q2/H2. The offsetting discovery is that the theme has quietly become international: WPIL's overseas revenue roughly doubled to INR 386cr, about 77% of consolidated, on PCI Africa's first full execution quarter plus Gruppo Aturia MENA demand, lifting consolidated EBITDA margin to 15.04%. EIEL carries an all-time-high order book (~6x revenue); WABAG on desalination/technology; JISLJALEQS/JISLDVREQS and MAHEPC add micro-irrigation and water-efficiency equipment; EMSLIMITED/SPMLINFRA/JASH/DENTA/ELECTCAST/AWHCL add sewerage, control equipment and ductile-iron piping. Execution conversion, not order intake, remains the binding constraint.
themes.driver: JJM/AMRUT fund releases unlocking billing (WPIL's INR 300-350cr receivable is the tracer); FY27 order inflow; desalination + NTPC BESS EPC ramp; international Africa/MENA execution.
